name: Buffer Over-read
principle: The product reads through an index, pointer, length, or string operation that can reference memory after the targeted buffer. This can disclose adjacent memory, leak addresses/secrets, or crash on invalid memory.
detection_signals: for/while loop reads buf[i] or *(p+i) with bound from untrusted length field and no check against buffer size
memcpy(dst, src, len) or memmove(dst, src, len) where len can exceed the actual readable size of src
printf("%s", buf), strlen(buf), strcpy(dst, buf), or strcmp(buf, x) on a char array not proven NUL-terminated
strncpy(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) followed by %s/strlen/strcpy use of dst without dst[sizeof(dst)-1]='\0'
pointer increment/read pattern *p++ or p[offset] inside loop without p < buf + buf_len guard
structure/protocol length field such as msgLength used to copy/read msgBody without validating msgLength <= received_body_len
negative_signals: read index guarded by i < buffer_len where buffer_len is the actual allocated/readable size
length field validated with len <= sizeof(buf) or len <= received_len before every read/copy
string buffer explicitly terminated after bounded copy: dst[sizeof(dst)-1] = '\0'
bounded string APIs use explicit maximum readable length, e.g. strnlen(buf, sizeof(buf)) or printf("%.*s", (int)len, buf)
memcpy/memmove length uses min(len, src_available) and src_available tracks actual source bytes
false_defense_traps: Trusting packet/header msgLength without comparing it to actual received body length
Using strncpy(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) and assuming it always appends NUL
Checking destination capacity only while the source buffer may be shorter than the requested read length
Assuming an out-of-bounds read is harmless because it does not write memory
Validating len for one buffer but then reusing it to read a different smaller buffer
verification_focus: Can any read index, pointer, copy length, or string scan advance past the end of the source buffer?

consequence_chains.trigger: inconsistent or untrusted length field exceeds actual buffer contents
consequence_chains.consequence: out-of-bounds read leaks memory or crashes

consequence_chains.trigger: missing NUL terminator reaches printf/strlen/%s string scan
consequence_chains.consequence: read continues past buffer end and may disclose adjacent memory

consequence_chains.trigger: over-read bytes are returned, logged, or printed
leaked memory addresses defeat ASLR before exploiting another memory error
consequence_chains.consequence: bypass protection mechanism and improve code-execution reliability

patch_principle: Validate all external length fields against actual received/readable buffer size before reading.
Bound every read by the source buffer size, not only the destination size.
Ensure fixed-size C strings are NUL-terminated before %s/strlen/strcpy-style APIs.
Use explicit-length APIs such as strnlen, snprintf with precision, or checked spans/slices.
Add fuzzing and ASan/Valgrind coverage for oversized lengths and unterminated strings.

minimal_examples.safe: for (i=0; i<msg->msgLength && i<body_len && i<sizeof(out)-1; i++) out[i] = msg->msgBody[i];
